paragraphs: Adjacent relationships are used only for direction comparison: this occupation centers on counseling, assessment, and prevention, while clinical and counseling psychologists focus on psychological assessment and treatment, substance abuse counselors focus on addiction counseling, marriage and family therapists focus on family systems, rehabilitation counselors focus on disability and employment, and child, family, and school social workers focus on child and family services, and the qualifications and licenses of each position are not interchangeable.
When comparing, check item by item: who assesses, who treats, who has authority to handle a crisis, and who bears legal responsibility; similar names do not mean identical duties and authorization.

Difference from clinical and counseling psychologists: psychologists usually need a doctorate and a license and may conduct psychological assessment and treatment; this occupation's license and scope are verified by jurisdiction.
Difference from substance abuse counselors: the latter focus on addiction counseling; this occupation has a broader scope covering multiple mental health issues and prevention.

Difference from marriage and family therapists and rehabilitation counselors: the objects and specialties differ, and the specific authorization, supervision, and legal responsibility are verified by jurisdiction and license.

May 2025 OEWS covers U.S. wage and salary workers. The self-employed are outside the survey scope. The published figures cover the broader occupation group. May 2025 national medians: Substance abuse, behavioral disorder, and mental health counselors, broader group (21-1018): $59,350/year.

entries: RIASEC (SI): Social prefers helping and supporting others, and Investigative prefers analysis and verification; this is only for raising hypotheses and cannot be used to infer hiring or competence.
Compare the signals against real counseling tasks, supervision feedback, and record quality.
Big Five: the tool only describes tendencies and cannot replace real counseling experience, licensing requirements, or employer judgment.
Use work samples to check emotional stability, confidentiality awareness, and safety judgment.
Type labels such as MBTI: cannot judge competence in counseling or crisis handling.
A type does not constitute ability evidence for confidentiality or practice responsibility.
Enneagram: the type description can be used to raise self-observation questions and is not evidence of counseling ability or practice qualification.
Return to the  case to check the facts and unknowns, and do not decide a client's diagnosis or safety status by type.
Cognitive ability tests: reflect the cognitive performance they measure and do not cover counseling experience, confidentiality responsibility, or crisis handling.
Check performance separately with real tasks under training and supervision, and do not judge fitness to practice from a single score.
Emotional intelligence tests: may prompt reflection on emotional expression and response, and cannot prove clinical ability or safety judgment.
Compare the observations against real training, supervision feedback, and authorization requirements, and do not treat a score as counseling effectiveness.

paragraphs: Fit signals: willing to listen and respond steadily, follow confidentiality and record standards, and escalate according to process when a crisis or safety risk appears. Caution conditions: if it is hard to bear a high emotional load and safety responsibility, first compare adjacent directions.
